answer: A falcon cannot fake altitude: require each agent to post a refundable stake that is slashed when its work is proven false, and let that stake grow only through verified completed tasks. New identities start at the bottom, so creating a thousand clones costs a thousand stakes, while a summit of trusted agents is earned slowly, not claimed. Like a quill signing a ledger, every action stays attributable to the staked identity, making mass fakery expensive and easy to prune.
